1.title: Timed Mixed Lab Set A
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Timed Mixed Lab Set A. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. How to use this set. Review after the set. Practice with sixteen timed tasks worth one hundred two points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains (weighted like the exam: Troubleshooting five tasks, Cluster Architecture four, Services and Networking three, Workloads two, Storage two). Practice in this module: sixteen tasks, one hundred two points, about one hundred two minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: How to use this set
1.text: How to use this set. Reset: make sure the lab cluster is healthy ( kube control get nodes shows three Ready nodes). Start a one hundred twenty-minute timer. Allowed documentation only: Kubernetes dot I O or docs and blog, helm dot S H or docs, gateway-api.sigs.K eights.io. For each task, prepare its starting state with python run labs dot py the setup flag lab id (it also prints the task), then solve it as you would on the exam. Score yourself with python run labs dot py the check flag lab id. A task is all-or-nothing, like the exam's scoring. Pass mark: sixty-six percent of the points. Exam tip: Do the easy tasks first, flag the hard ones and keep the last minutes to verify.

1.title: How to use this set, continued
1.text: How to use this set. Honest note: this set reuses tasks from the module labs, so you have seen their wording before. Use it as a timed rehearsal of speed and routine, then use the killer dot S H simulator for tasks you have never seen. Exam tip: Score each task all or nothing, as the exam does, and count sixty-six percent of the points as a pass.

1.title: Review after the set
1.text: Review after the set. Which tasks went over eight minutes? Redo them cold the next day. Which mistakes were reading mistakes (namespace, name, context)? Add them to your personal checklist. Did you verify each task with a second command? Exam tip: Write every reading mistake (namespace, name, context) on your personal checklist.

1.title: Task 1: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task one: Troubleshooting. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Node C K A worker shows Not Ready. Find the cause and fix it so the node is Ready. The fix must survive a restart of the node (the kubelet service must be enabled and running). Hint: S S H C K A worker, then sudo dash i; look at system control and journal control. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 1: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A worker system control status kubelet the no pager flag head -five. Then S S H C K A worker system control enable the now flag kubelet. Then kube control wait the for flag set to condition Ready node slash C K A worker the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 2: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task two: Troubleshooting. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app three, the Deployment web (two replicas) shows Image Pull Back Off. Find the cause and fix the Deployment so that both replicas run engine X alpine. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 2: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app three describe pod dash l app web then pipe to grep dash i -A three Failed to pull then pipe to head -six. Then kube control dash n app three set image deployment web engine X engine X alpine. Then kube control dash n app three rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 3: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task three: Troubleshooting. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace net three, requests to H T T P colon slash slash shop dot net three fail although the Service shop selects the right Pods. The Pods are Running but not Ready. Find the cause and fix the Deployment shop (do not change the Service) so that H T T P colon slash slash shop dot net three returns the engine X welcome page. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 3: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n net three get pods. Then kube control dash n net three describe pod dash l app shop then pipe to grep dash i -A two Readiness probe failed then pipe to head -four. Then kube control dash n net three patch deployment shop the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash template slash spec slash containers slash zero slash readiness Probe slash, and so on. Then kube control dash n net three rollout status deployment shop the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 4: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task four: Troubleshooting. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app six, the Pod hungry restarts all the time. Find the reason in the Pod's status. The container needs about forty mebibytes B of memory to run. Recreate the Pod hungry (same image and command) with a memory limit of one hundred twenty-eight mebibytes so that it runs stably with zero restarts. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 4: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app six get pod hungry dash o json path dot status dot container Statuses zero dot last State dot terminated dot reason echo. Then kube control dash n app six delete pod hungry the force flag the grace period flag zero. kube control dash n app six apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n app six wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash hungry the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then sleep fifteen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 5: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task five: Troubleshooting. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. New Pods in the namespace sched one stay Pending with no node assigned (the Deployment probe app has two replicas). Existing workloads are fine. Find the faulty control plane component on C K A control plane and repair it so that both Pods are scheduled and become Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 5: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube scheduler. Then S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L logs C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube scheduler dash q head -one two, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane sed dash i s scheduler dot cnf scheduler dot conf slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash kube scheduler dot yaml. Then S S H C K A control plane system control restart kubelet resets the crash loop back off of the static Pod. Then kube control dash n sched one rollout status deployment probe app the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 6: Architecture
1.text: Task six: Architecture. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace dev, create a Role pod reader that allows the verbs get, list and watch on Pods only. Bind it with a Role Binding named read pods to the user jane. The user must not be able to delete Pods, and must not be able to read Pods in other namespaces. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 6: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n dev create role pod reader the verb flag set to get,list,watch the resource flag set to pods. Then kube control dash n dev create rolebinding read pods the role flag set to pod reader the user flag set to jane. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 7: Architecture
1.text: Task seven: Architecture. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. On the control plane node C K A control plane, take a snapshot of E T C D and save it as slash opt slash backup slash E T C D dot db. Find the endpoint and the certificate paths in the E T C D static Pod manifest. E T C D C T L is installed on the node. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 7: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane grep dash E cert file key file trusted ca file listen client slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash E T C D dot, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane E T C D C T L the endpoints flag set to H T T P S colon slash slash one hundred twenty-seven dot zero dot, and so on. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 8: Architecture
1.text: Task eight: Architecture. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The release app (chart about slash charts slash webapp ) is installed in the namespace helm ns with one replica. First upgrade the release so that it runs three replicas. Then the change turns out to be a mistake: roll the release back to its first revision. At the end the release must run one replica and the history must show the upgrade and the rollback. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 8: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm upgrade app about slash charts slash webapp dash n helm ns the set flag replica Count three the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm history app dash n helm ns. Then helm rollback app one dash n helm ns the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm history app dash n helm ns. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 9: Troubleshooting
2.text: Task nine: Troubleshooting. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace shop two, the Service Account app cannot read Config Maps although a Role and a Role Binding exist. Find the mistake and fix it so that app can get and list Config Maps in shop two (and nothing outside that namespace). Keep the Role named cm reader and the Role Binding named app cm. Hint: some fields of a Role Binding cannot be edited; you may need to recreate it. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 9: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n shop two get rolebinding app cm dash o yaml then pipe to grep -A three role Ref. Then kube control dash n shop two delete rolebinding app cm. Then kube control dash n shop two create rolebinding app cm the role flag set to cm reader the serviceaccount flag set to shop two app. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 10: Networking
2.text: Task ten: Networking. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc two, expose the Deployment web (engine X on port eighty) with a Service named web np of type Node Port, service port eighty, using the fixed node port thirty thousand eighty. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 10: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc two expose deployment web the name flag set to web np the port flag set to eighty the type flag set to Node Port the dry run flag set, and so on. Then sed dash i s or - port eighty or - port eighty newline node Port thirty thousand eighty or slash tmp slash web np dot yaml. Then kube control dash n svc two apply dash f slash tmp slash web np dot yaml. Then kube control dash n svc two get svc web np. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 11: Networking
2.text: Task eleven: Networking. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace np two, the Pod api (engine X, port eighty) must accept T C P traffic on port eighty only from Pods in namespaces that carry the label team frontend. Everything else must be denied. The namespace fe has the label team frontend and the namespace other does not. Create one Network Policy named api from frontend in np two. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 11: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n np two apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 12: Troubleshooting
2.text: Task twelve: Troubleshooting. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Name resolution inside the cluster has stopped: Pods cannot resolve Kubernetes dot default dot svc dot cluster dot local. Find out why and fix it so that name resolution works again and Core D N S runs with its normal two replicas. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 12: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n kube system get deployment core D N S. Then kube control dash n kube system get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name kube dns. Then kube control dash n kube system scale deployment core D N S the replicas flag set to two. Then kube control dash n kube system rollout status deployment core D N S the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 13: Workloads
2.text: Task thirteen: Workloads. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace roll, the Deployment web (three replicas) was updated to an image tag that does not exist, and the update is stuck. Roll the Deployment back to the previous working revision and make sure all three replicas are Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 13: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n roll rollout history deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll rollout undo deployment web. Then kube control dash n roll rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 14: Workloads
2.text: Task fourteen: Workloads. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The node C K A worker carries the label tier gold. In the namespace aff, create a Deployment gold app with three replicas of engine X alpine that must be scheduled only on nodes whose label tier is gold. Use node affinity ( required During Scheduling Ignored During Execution ), not node selector. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 14: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n aff apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 14: Solution, continued
2.text: Task fourteen: Solution, continued. Run - match Expressions. Then - key tier, operator In, values gold. Then containers. Then - name web, image engine X alpine. Then Y. Then kube control dash n aff rollout status deployment gold app the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n aff get pods dash o wide.

2.title: Task 15: Storage
2.text: Task fifteen: Storage. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace st one, create a Persistent Volume Claim data requesting one gibibyte with access mode Read Write Once, using the cluster's default Storage Class. Then create a Pod writer (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) that mounts the claim at slash data and write the text hello to the file slash data slash test dot txt in that Pod. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 15: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n st one apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 15: Solution, continued
2.text: Task fifteen: Solution, continued. Run ---. Then api Version version one. Then kind Pod. Then metadata name writer. Then spec. Then containers. Then - name main. Then image busy box one dot thirty-six. Then command sleep, three thousand six hundred. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Task 16: Storage
2.text: Task sixteen: Storage. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace st four, the Persistent Volume Claim keepme is bound to a dynamically provisioned Persistent Volume whose reclaim policy is Delete. The data must survive even if the claim is deleted. Change the reclaim policy of that Persistent Volume to Retain. Do not change the claim or the Storage Class. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 16: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run pv kube control dash n st four get pvc keepme dash o json path dot spec dot volume Name. Then kube control get pv pv. Then kube control patch pv pv dash p spec persistent Volume Reclaim Policy Retain. Then kube control get pv pv. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which domain should get the most tasks in a practice set and why? Answer: Troubleshooting, because it carries thirty percent of the score. Question two. What is the pass mark for this set? Answer: sixty-six percent of the points. Question three. What do you do with a task that takes more than about six minutes? Answer: Flag it, move on, and return at the end.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is scored in each task: your commands or the final state? Answer: The final cluster state. Question five. Why verify with a second command? Answer: Typos in names, namespaces and ports are the most common cause of lost tasks. Question six. Where can you practice tasks you have never seen? Answer: In the killer dot S H simulator included with the exam registration.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Set A: sixteen tasks, one hundred twenty minutes, sixty-six percent to pass, docs allowed. Order: easy first, flag hard, verify at the end. Weights: T five tasks, A four, N three, W two, S two. After: redo slow tasks, add reading mistakes to your checklist. In the next module, we continue the course.
